classification.difficultyReason: Scale mass in the same ratio as beam length and round the resulting mass to the nearest kilogram.

content.prompt: The mass $m$ kilograms of a steel beam of uniform cross-section is directly proportional to its length $\ell$ metres. If a $6$ m section of the beam has a mass of $400$ kg, what will be the mass, to the nearest kilogram, of a section $5$ m long?

answer.worked:
Since $m\propto\ell$,
$$\begin{align*}m &= k\ell\\400 &= 6k\\k &= \frac{400}{6}=\frac{200}{3}\\m &= \frac{200}{3}\ell\end{align*}$$
When $\ell=5$,
$$\begin{align*}m &= \frac{200}{3}\times5\\m &= \frac{1000}{3}\\m &\approx 333\text{ kg}\end{align*}$$
The mass is $333$ kg to the nearest kilogram.
